newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria bridles at idea of Libyan mediation.
newsitem.headline: Algeria bridles at idea of Libyan mediation.

text.p: The Algerian government on Thursday snubbed beforehand a proposal for Libyan mediation between the Algerian authorities and their radical Islamist enemies to end the country's five-year-old civil strife.

In a 65 line commentary by the official Algerian news agency APS, mirroring the government's stand, Algiers bluntly told Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi that it did not want to be an "outlet" for his beleaguered regime to step into the limelight on the world stage.

Algeria was reacting to a report by the official Libyan news agency JANA saying on Monday that Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had asked Gaddafi to meditate between the fundamentalist leaders and the Algerian government in order to hammer out a peaceful solution to the conflict.
"The Libyan authorities up to today have not denied this information, suggesting they are ready to interfere in Algeria's internal affairs," said APS.
The Algerian government blasted Gaddafi in 1993 when he referred to the FIS's jailed leader Abassi Madani as "brother", and then lodged an official protest through the Libyan envoy to Algiers.
APS warned on Thursday that the Libyan leader would be the loser if he pursued a double game.
Repeating Algeria's refusal at previous attempts to mediate in its conflict, APS added:
"Algeria has barred itself from interfering in other countries' affairs. The least it can expect in return from its neighbours is that they do the same".

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence locking Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS had taken a commanding lead.
